items.title: Roy McCurdy interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] My name is Monk Rowe, and we’re very pleased to have with us jazz drummer Roy McCurdy. Welcome. [INTERVIEWEE] Oh, thank you.

ctx.x: Drummer Roy McCurdy has worked in a variety of jazz settings. A native of Rochester, NY, he first recorded with the Jazz Brothers, a group co-led by Chuck and Gap Mangione. In the early 60’s he drove the combos of Sonny Rollins, Bobby Timmons and Betty Carter. Cannonball Adderley called on Roy in 1965 and for the next ten years he was part of one of the hottest groups in jazz. Cannon’s biggest hits were recorded during this time, including “Mercy, Mercy” and “Country Preacher.” In the latter 70’s, Roy worked with…
Roy was interviewed by Monk Rowe in New York on November 16, 1995.
We are filming today for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive here in New York City. My name is Monk Rowe, and we’re very pleased to have with us jazz drummer Roy McCurdy. Welcome.
